 ## [Unreleased]
 
+## [0.36.3] - 2026-11-14
+
+### Fixed
+
+- A `params` string sent as a JSON string literal, with its quotes and `\n` escapes, reaches the program decoded, also when the program declares a string input (#368). Such a program got the encoded text, so a PR body passed to `gh pr create --body` started with `"` and showed `\n` instead of line breaks. A quoted string that is not valid JSON is passed through unchanged.
+
 ## [0.36.2] - 2026-11-13
 
 ### Added

-The tool schema gives `params` an explicit JSON type for every kind of value, so clients send objects and arrays as JSON rather than as encoded strings. If a client still sends a JSON string, Pit decodes a string holding a JSON object or array when the declared input type does not accept strings; a program that declares a string input receives the string unchanged. Clients that sample arguments against a strict JSON schema send `null` for options the model left out, so a `null` value for `params`, `label`, `functionId`, `saveOnly`, or `timeoutMs` counts as omitted.
+The tool schema gives `params` an explicit JSON type for every kind of value, so clients send objects and arrays as JSON rather than as encoded strings. If a client still sends a JSON string, Pit decodes a string holding a JSON object or array when the declared input type does not accept strings; a program that declares a string input receives such a string unchanged. A string that is itself a JSON string literal, quotes and `\n` escapes included, is decoded for every input, so a string input receives the text with real line breaks; a quoted string that is not valid JSON is passed through. Clients that sample arguments against a strict JSON schema send `null` for options the model left out, so a `null` value for `params`, `label`, `functionId`, `saveOnly`, or `timeoutMs` counts as omitted.
 
 Providers that support grammar-constrained tool input, such as OpenAI's Responses API, receive the tool with a grammar like Pi's codemode tool, and the model writes the program as raw text in `code` instead of a JSON-escaped string. Other providers keep the JSON schema. In raw text, an optional first line sets the other parameters as one JSON object, `// @pit: {"label": "Check status", "timeoutMs": 60000, "params": {"files": ["a.ts"]}}`. Pit moves those values into the call and leaves an empty first line, so diagnostics keep the line numbers as written. The line works with any provider. Setting the same parameter both there and as an argument is an error.
